summary:
Región del Maule stands under the national framework of Chile, where legal gender recognition has operated since Gender Identity Law 21,120 came into force on 27 December 2019. Adults may change their registered name and sex on request to the Civil Registry without therapy or sex-reassignment surgery, so a traveller's papers can be brought into line with their presentation. People aged 14 to 18 must apply to family courts with psychosocial and family-context antecedents. Those under 14 cannot use the law, although the statute recognises them as transgender; on 9 April 2025 the Constitutional Court declared the 'over 14 years old' wording inapplicable as unconstitutional in a case brought by the mother of a 10-year-old trans girl, and that ruling applies only to that case. Birth certificates offer a third sex option for intersex children.

Anti-discrimination protection rests on the Zamudio Law of 2012, which covers sexual orientation and gender identity, was extended to gender expression in 2018, and treats hate-crime motivation as an aggravating criminal circumstance; individuals may also file anti-discrimination lawsuits. Same-sex marriage and joint adoption have been legal since 10 March 2022, under a law approved on 9 December 2021, following civil unions available since 2015.

Entry and removal rules reference gender identity. The Migration and Immigration Law of 11 April 2021 bans arbitrary discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity and offers protection to LGBT immigrants seeking asylum. Article 10 provides that recognised asylum seekers may be granted complementary protection, and no foreigner holding complementary protection may be expelled or returned to a country where their right to life, physical integrity or personal freedom is at risk on grounds including sexual orientation or gender identity.

Detention carries specific rules. Gendarmería de Chile's national director signed a protocol guaranteeing the gender identity of trans detainees, providing placement by assumed gender, segmented housing and entry examinations, with a standing committee of Gendarmería and undersecretariat representatives overseeing implementation, including access rules for trans visitors.

Access to care is established at national level. The public health system has funded sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy since 2013, and a 2011 Ministry of Health circular obliges care centres to register transgender patients by their social name. Circular 7 of June 2024 suggested deferring the initiation of new gonadotropin-releasing hormone blockers and cross-sex hormone therapy in adolescents until national guidelines are published, and the Medical College noted that physicians may still prescribe. On 9 January 2025 the Constitutional Court, by seven votes to three, annulled section 46 of the 2025 Budget Law, which had barred the Ministry of Health from financing hormone therapies for trans children and adolescents. In November 2025 Congress defunded the Ministry of Social Development's Gender Identity Support Program through the 2026 Budget Law, but the Ministry of Health-run programme continues to provide support in medical centres; the Crece con Orgullo programme has operated since 2023 for children and adolescents aged 3 to 17.

Transphobic violence remains documented. A young trans man was murdered in 2023 in a killing covered up for 24 hours and described in national reporting as Chile's largest hate crime; the perpetrator, an acquaintance, confessed. In September 2021 a 20-year-old trans man and his girlfriend were beaten with bottles and clubs and held against their will for close to an hour at a Santiago hotel, where the attacker said he wanted to kill the victim.

Restrictive proposals are active but non-binding. On 15 May 2025 the Chamber of Deputies approved the CEI 57 commission report, 56 votes to 30 with 6 abstentions, a non-binding recommendation to eliminate the Gender Identity Support Program, restrict minors' progressive autonomy, ban hormonal treatment for minors and repeal the circular protecting gender identity in schools.
tangentialFactors:
The national anti-discrimination picture is moving in the opposite direction to the legal framework. Movilh's XXIV Annual Human Rights Report records 3,620 cases of LGBTIQ+ discrimination in 2025, an increase of 27.1%, the highest annual figure on record and 23% of all cases registered over 24 years; 2,847 cases were recorded in 2024, up 78.7%. Enforcement machinery is not dormant: in 2025 a criminal court issued the country's first lesbophobic-femicide conviction under Article 390 ter of the penal code.

The 2025-26 rollback is legislative rather than judicial. Outright International's Chile overview, last updated 12 March 2026, records that Congress excluded the Gender Identity Support Program from the 2026 budget bill, and that a parliamentary commission report approved in May 2025, following the UK Cass Report, portrays gender-affirming initiatives as a threat to children's development and recommends restricting access. Movilh's report documents the same sequence: removal of the programme from the 2026 budget, health-ministry circular N8 restricting it for minors, and legislative initiative CEI-57 against the rights of trans children.

Comparison with the parent framework matters for expectations on the ground: the Chamber of Deputies vote of 15 May 2025 recommended repealing the school circular and banning hormonal treatment for minors, but a non-binding report does not alter the statutes, the court rulings or the health-funding position currently in force.

outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory carries a finding specific to the Región del Maule. The Wikipedia entry for the Maule Region yielded no usable trans-related content, and Movilh's report records a per-region case share without publishing a figure for this region. All statements above therefore describe the national framework and national enforcement under which the region sits; regional policing, facilities, health provision and recorded incidents in the Maule are unresolved and not sourced here.

The reach of the Constitutional Court's 9 April 2025 ruling on the 'over 14 years old' wording is stated in the sources as applying only to the case in which it was issued; whether other under-14 applications have succeeded is unresolved and not sourced.

Movilh's report cites health-ministry circular N8 restricting the Gender Identity Support Program for minors, while the parent framework refers to Circular 7 of June 2024 on deferring new hormone initiation. Whether these are the same instrument is unresolved and not sourced.

Outright International's overview was last updated 12 March 2026 and Movilh's report was published in March 2026; both postdate other material in this inventory, and no source confirms whether the CEI 57 recommendations or the 2026 budget exclusion have since been acted on.
